body.translated_text: The hymn to <s>Śiva</s> composed by <s>Śrī Laṅkeśvara</s>.

children.text: gale kalitakālima prakaṭitendu bhālasthale vināṭitajaṭotkaraṃ rucirapāṇipāthoruhe /
children.translated_text: With darkness adorning the throat, with the moon displayed on the forehead, with splendid masses of upswept matted locks, with a beautiful hand [holding] a water-lotus,

children.text: udañcitakapālakaṃ jaghanasīmni saṃdarśitadvipājinamanukṣaṇaṃ kimapi dhāma vandāmahe // LSiv_1 //
children.translated_text: with a raised skull-cup, with elephant hide displayed at the hip — we venerate that ineffable radiance, moment by moment.
Shining with white splendor atop the bull, whose radiant glory puts to shame the pride arising from the whiteness of <s>Kubera's</s> mountain (<s>Kailāsa</s>),

children.text: rucirapunarumākucopacitakuṅkumai rañjitaṃ gajājinavirājitaṃ vṛjinabhaṅgabījaṃ bhaje // LSiv_2 //
children.translated_text: yet reddened again by the <s>kuṅkuma</s> (saffron) from the embrace of <s>Umā's</s> bosom, resplendent with elephant hide — I worship that seed of the destruction of sin.
By the radiance streaming from the three risen fiery eyes and by the mingling of the moon's digits, day and night,

I praise <s>Mṛḍa</s> (Śiva, the gracious one), whose trembling crest holds the playful waves of the celestial river (<s>Gaṅgā</s>) delighting in sporting through the forest of his opened matted locks.

children.text: vihāya kamalālayāvilasitāni vidyunnaṭīviḍambanapaṭūni me viharaṇaṃ vidhattāṃ manaḥ /
children.translated_text: Abandoning the allurements of the lotus-dwelling one (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) and the clever imitations of the dancing lightning, may my mind find its abode
in the <s>Kapardin</s> (the matted-locked <s>Śiva</s>), who wears the crescent moon as his crest-jewel, whose elephant hide hangs at his hip, the Supreme Being (<s>Brahman</s>).
Your palace threshold is thronged by <s>Maghavan</s> (<s>Indra</s>) and the other gods, whose crown-tips are broken from striking against the terrifying door-bar;

children.text: vrajema bhavadantikaṃ prakṛtimetya paiśācikīṃ kimityamarasaṃpadaḥ pramathanātha nāthāma he // LSiv_5 //
children.translated_text: shall we, assuming the nature of <s>piśācas</s> (ghouls), approach your presence — why should we seek the wealth of the immortals? O Lord of the <s>Pramathas</s>, O Lord!
We wish for some mountain [<s>Kailāsa</s>] whose flowering and fruit-laden trees are plundered by the <s>Pramatha</s> maidens devoted to your worship;
enough with <s>Meru</s>, whose beauty consists merely of the scattered flowers from the hair of <s>Siddha</s> women reclining on its terrace-platforms.

children.text: na jātu hara yātu me viṣayadurvilāsaṃ mano manobhavakathāstu me na ca manorathātithyabhūḥ /
children.translated_text: O <s>Hara</s>! May my mind never go toward the base enjoyment of sense objects; let the tales of the god of love find no hospitality in me, nor desires become my guests;

children.text: sphuratsurataraṅgiṇītaṭakuṭīrakoṭau vasannaye śiva devāniśaṃ tava bhavāni pūjāparaḥ // LSiv_7 //
children.translated_text: dwelling at the peak of a hut on the bank of the sparkling celestial river, O <s>Śiva</s>! O God! May I always be devoted to the worship of <s>Bhavānī</s> (your consort).
Nourished by the sprinkling of thick masses of spray from the fine trembling rows of waves of the celestial river that serves as his ornament,

children.text: maheśvarasuradrumasphuritasajjaṭāmañjarī namajjanaphalapradā mama nu hanta bhūyādiyam // LSiv_8 //
children.translated_text: may this cluster of luxuriant matted locks of <s>Maheśvara</s>, the wish-fulfilling tree, bestow fruit upon those who bow — ah, may it truly be so for me!
Of <s>Paśupati</s> (the Lord of creatures), the all-Self, whose row of senses is turned back from contact with external objects, who is absorbed in <s>samādhi</s> (meditation),
I worship the crescent moon upon his head — a wish-fulfilling tree at the river-bank hut of the celestial stream — being contemplated by a young celibate student.
May this mind of mine, plunging into the dense thicket of matted locks along the stream of pure water-drops from your celestial river,
attain the likeness of the assembly of ascetics delighting in the forest of trees on the bank of the most excellent river — O Lord, radiant as pure jasmine!

body.translated_text: Thus ends the hymn to <s>Śiva</s> composed by <s>Śrī Laṅkeśvara</s>.
